# Sujiko: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `sujiko.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.39) and `sujiko-rules.soar` (14 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_logic.py`, function `task`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . sujiko.soar --seed 1 --cap 100000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . sujiko.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py sujiko init-sujiko.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world (for the state checks).

World: init-sujiko.world (a 3x3 grid of locations and four clue blocks, each above the four locations around it).

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, 16 Nov 2026)

Every plan below was replayed independently by `check_plan.py`, which applies the instructor's statements directly to the world file.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`) | fail-sujiko: goal true, failure true; final-sujiko: goal true, failure false; init-sujiko: goal false, failure false. All as the instructor intended (a fail state counts as lost even when the goal also holds). |
| Seeds 1–3, library v2.39 (failed moves rejected): 1/3 correct | 1: 3 writes, 100,000 decisions: goal does not hold (stopped at the cap: a dead end, every remaining write rejected; see PILOT.md)<br>2: 3 writes, 100,000 decisions: goal does not hold (stopped at the cap: a dead end, every remaining write rejected; see PILOT.md)<br>3: 4 writes, 10,209 decisions: goal holds |
| Seeds 1–3, library v2.37 (failed moves worst): 0/3 correct | 1: 4 writes, 3,402 decisions: action 4 reaches a losing state<br>2: 4 writes, 3,266 decisions: action 4 reaches a losing state<br>3: 4 writes, 1,952 decisions: action 4 reaches a losing state |

The v2.37 failures are library behaviour, not translation errors; v2.39 changed the library because of them. See "Logic puzzles" in `../../PILOT.md`.

## Translation

- grouping: the locations under one block (the under relation of the world file); target: that block's value.
- Operator write (argument1 = the location, argument2 = number-k for k from 1 to 9).

## Assumption ledger

| ID | Reading |
|---|---|
| A-W1 | The action takes the location and a number object (number-1 to number-N): operator arguments are objects under the conventions; the effect gives the location ^value k. |
| A-W2 | "empty" (the value is absent) tests absence and decides legality, so it is a maintained one-argument relation, removed by write; "filled" (value more than zero) is expanded in place. |
| A-W3 | "all locations are filled" is expanded over the locations of the world file, so the goal test is positive. |
| A-W4 | "The solution has N steps." is checked against the plans, not used. |
